transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Because there is standing water next to your plug sockets, this is an immediate electrical hazard. Please do not use the dishwasher or touch those sockets until a qualified electrician has inspected them; if you are unsure, call one now. Regarding the leak: it is most likely caused by water escaping from the door area (often due to a blocked spray arm hitting something, or a damaged seal) or an internal hose/pump leak. To help narrow this down safely: 1. 2. Open the door and check the rubber seal around the tub edge for damage or debris caught in it.
3. Check that nothing in your racks is blocking the spray arms from spinning freely by hand.

omg the water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor and the socket is on the wall right next to the dishwasher. the door seal looks ok to me tho. not sure how to check the spray arms, its still running what do i do

You need to switch off the power at your main fuse box (consumer unit) immediately. Do not touch the plug, the extension lead, or the sockets while they are wet or if water is touching them. This is a serious electric shock hazard. Once you have isolated the electricity and it is safe to do so, please try to find the model number on a sticker inside the door frame or on the side edge of the door. I need this to identify the correct repair parts for the leak (likely an internal pump seal or hose given the water volume).
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

ok i think rcd hasnt tripped. do i switch off the whole house power?? i dont know the model its my landlords machine, never looked. also housemate put fairy washing up liquid in cos we ran out of tablets, theres loads of bubbles coming out the door

Yes, please switch off the power at your main fuse box (consumer unit) immediately. Since the RCD hasn't tripped and water is near your extension lead and wall socket, this is still an active electric shock hazard. Do not touch any plugs or sockets while they are wet. The 'fairy' washing-up liquid has created excessive foam that is overflowing from the door. This is a common issue when using hand-wash liquid in a dishwasher; it creates too many bubbles for the machine to handle, causing them to spill out like soap suds. Once you have isolated the power and it is safe to approach without touching wet electrical items, please soak up as much of the foam from the floor with towels and drain the excess suds from the bottom of the dishwasher (you may need to tilt it carefully if accessible, or use a sponge). Because water has reached your sockets and extension lead, you must have a qualified electrician check them before using them again. Once the immediate danger is managed, please try to find the model number on a sticker inside the door frame so we can advise on clearing the foam from the machine itself.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
